experiment: Optical Fibre Numerical Aperture - Question Bank
description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Optical Fibre Numerical Aperture

questions.question: What is the basic principle of optical fibre transmission?
questions.explanation: Light signals are confined and guided inside an optical fibre by continuous total internal reflections.

questions.question: The central light-guiding region of an optical fibre is called:
questions.explanation: The core is the inner cylindrical optical medium through which light travels.

questions.question: The layer surrounding the core is called:
questions.explanation: The cladding wraps around the core with a slightly lower refractive index to facilitate TIR.

questions.question: The refractive index of the core is generally:
questions.explanation: TIR requires light to propagate from a medium of higher refractive index (n₁) to lower index (n₂), so n₁ > n₂.

questions.question: TIR stands for:
questions.explanation: Total Internal Reflection is the optical phenomenon where 100% of incident light is reflected back into the denser medium.

questions.question: For TIR, light must travel from:
options: Optically denser to optically rarer medium
questions.answer: Optically denser to optically rarer medium
questions.correct_option: Optically denser to optically rarer medium
questions.explanation: TIR can only take place when light travels from higher optical density (core) towards lower optical density (cladding).

questions.question: The angle of incidence for TIR must be:
questions.explanation: When θi > θc, refraction into the rarer medium cannot satisfy Snell's law, causing total reflection.

questions.question: Optical fibre is commonly used for:
questions.explanation: Optical fibres form the backbone of modern global high-speed telecommunications and internet infrastructure.

questions.question: Which material is commonly used to make optical fibres?
questions.explanation: High-purity silica glass (SiO₂) or transparent polymers (PMMA) are standard optical fibre materials.

questions.question: A single-mode fibre has:
options: A very small core and mainly one propagation mode
questions.answer: A very small core and mainly one propagation mode
questions.correct_option: A very small core and mainly one propagation mode
questions.explanation: Single-mode fibres (core diameter ~8-10 µm) guide only the fundamental optical mode, eliminating modal dispersion.

questions.question: Multimode fibre generally has:
questions.explanation: Multimode fibres typically have larger core diameters (50 µm to 62.5 µm), allowing multiple ray propagation paths.

questions.question: Numerical aperture indicates the fibre's:
questions.explanation: NA = sin(θmax) characterizes the range of launch angles from which the fibre can accept and guide light.

questions.question: Acceptance angle is related to:
options: Maximum angle for light to enter and remain guided
questions.answer: Maximum angle for light to enter and remain guided
questions.correct_option: Maximum angle for light to enter and remain guided
questions.explanation: Acceptance angle θmax is the maximum semi-angle of the incident light cone that undergoes TIR at core-cladding boundary.

questions.question: The critical angle depends on:
options: Refractive indices of the two media
questions.answer: Refractive indices of the two media
questions.correct_option: Refractive indices of the two media
questions.explanation: The critical angle is determined by sin(θc) = n₂ / n₁.

questions.question: The outer protective layer of a fibre is generally called:
questions.explanation: The buffer coating and outer polymer jacket protect the fragile glass core/cladding against moisture and mechanical stress.

questions.question: In an optical fibre, light is guided mainly through the:
questions.explanation: The high refractive index core traps and propagates the optical wave.

questions.question: Optical fibre communication offers:
questions.explanation: Optical frequencies (~hundreds of Terahertz) support gigabits-to-terabits per second data transmission bandwidth.

questions.question: Optical fibres are immune to ordinary:
questions.explanation: Dielectric glass fibres do not conduct electrical current, making them completely immune to EMI and radio noise.

questions.question: A ray travelling exactly along the normal at a boundary has angle of incidence:
questions.explanation: Angle of incidence is measured relative to the normal; normal incidence means θ = 0°.

questions.question: The unit commonly used for refractive index is:
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v is a dimensionless ratio of two velocities.

questions.question: Snell's law relates:
questions.explanation: Snell's Law: n₁ sin(θ₁) = n₂ sin(θ₂).

questions.question: For an optical fibre with core index n1 and cladding index n2, guidance requires:
questions.explanation: Core must be optically denser than cladding to support TIR.

questions.question: Critical angle C at a core-cladding boundary satisfies:
questions.explanation: Setting refracted angle θ₂ = 90° in Snell's law gives n₁ sin(C) = n₂ sin(90°) => sin(C) = n₂/n₁.

questions.question: For air outside a fibre, numerical aperture is commonly given by:
questions.explanation: NA = n₀ sin(θmax) = √(n₁² - n₂²) when launching from air (n₀ = 1.0).

questions.question: Acceptance angle increases when NA:
questions.explanation: θmax = arcsin(NA); higher NA directly widens the acceptance cone angle.

questions.question: If n1 = n2, the ideal numerical aperture is:
questions.explanation: NA = √(n₁² - n₂²) = √(n₁² - n₁²) = 0; no refractive index contrast means zero light-guiding capability.

questions.question: Why does cladding have a lower refractive index than the core?
options: To enable total internal reflection at the interface
questions.answer: To enable total internal reflection at the interface
questions.correct_option: To enable total internal reflection at the interface
questions.explanation: Without a lower-index cladding, light would refract and leak out into surroundings.

questions.question: Which fibre is generally preferred for very long-distance, high-bandwidth links?
questions.explanation: Single-mode fibres provide extremely low attenuation and zero intermodal pulse dispersion over hundreds of kilometers.

questions.question: Step-index fibre means the refractive index of the core:
options: Is approximately constant and changes abruptly at the cladding
questions.answer: Is approximately constant and changes abruptly at the cladding
questions.correct_option: Is approximately constant and changes abruptly at the cladding
questions.explanation: Step-index profile features uniform core index n₁ with a sharp step change to n₂ at the cladding boundary.

questions.question: In a graded-index multimode fibre, core refractive index:
options: Gradually decreases away from the centre
questions.answer: Gradually decreases away from the centre
questions.correct_option: Gradually decreases away from the centre
questions.explanation: Parabolic grading curves outer rays back towards the axis, equalizing travel times across modes.

questions.question: Modal dispersion is especially associated with:
questions.explanation: Different modes take paths of different geometric lengths, spreading the optical pulse.

questions.question: Attenuation in fibre refers to:
options: Loss of optical power during propagation
questions.answer: Loss of optical power during propagation
questions.correct_option: Loss of optical power during propagation
questions.explanation: Attenuation (measured in dB/km) is signal power decay as photons travel through the fibre.

questions.question: One important cause of attenuation is:
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering (from density fluctuations) and material absorption are primary intrinsic losses.

questions.question: A connector in an optical system is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: Optical connectors provide low-loss, repeatable optical alignment between fibres and transmitter/receiver ports.

questions.question: If the refractive index of the core increases while cladding index stays fixed, NA generally:
questions.explanation: NA = √(n₁² - n₂²); increasing n₁ increases the radical value, raising NA.

questions.question: For TIR, the refracted ray at the boundary:
options: Does not enter the second medium as a propagating ray
questions.answer: Does not enter the second medium as a propagating ray
questions.correct_option: Does not enter the second medium as a propagating ray
questions.explanation: No propagating wave carries energy into the rarer medium (only a non-propagating evanescent field exists).

questions.question: The acceptance cone represents:
options: The range of input directions accepted by the fibre
questions.answer: The range of input directions accepted by the fibre
questions.correct_option: The range of input directions accepted by the fibre
questions.explanation: It is the 3D cone formed by rotating the maximum acceptance angle θmax about the core axis.

questions.question: Why is optical fibre useful in medical endoscopy?
options: It can transmit light/images through a flexible path
questions.answer: It can transmit light/images through a flexible path
questions.correct_option: It can transmit light/images through a flexible path
questions.explanation: Coherent fibre bundles allow illumination and visual inspection inside internal organs non-invasively.

questions.question: Compared with copper communication cables, fibre generally has:
options: Lower transmission loss over suitable long links and higher bandwidth
questions.answer: Lower transmission loss over suitable long links and higher bandwidth
questions.correct_option: Lower transmission loss over suitable long links and higher bandwidth
questions.explanation: Optical attenuation (~0.2 dB/km at 1550 nm) is orders of magnitude lower than electrical cable attenuation.

questions.question: A fibre's V-number (normalized frequency) depends on:
options: Core/cladding indices, core radius and wavelength
questions.answer: Core/cladding indices, core radius and wavelength
questions.correct_option: Core/cladding indices, core radius and wavelength
questions.explanation: V = (2π a / λ) √(n₁² - n₂²) = (2π a / λ) NA.

questions.question: If n1 = 1.50 and n2 = 1.48, the NA in air is approximately:
For n1 = 1.5 and n2 = 1.0, the critical angle is approximately:
If NA = 0.5 in air, the acceptance half-angle is approximately:
questions.explanation: sin(θmax) = NA = 0.5 => θmax = arcsin(0.5) = 30°.

questions.question: If the fibre core radius is increased while other parameters remain fixed, the normalized frequency V:
questions.explanation: V = (2π a / λ) NA is directly proportional to core radius a.

Why does single-mode fibre reduce modal dispersion?
options: Only one mode is primarily guided
It has no refractive index difference
questions.answer: Only one mode is primarily guided
questions.correct_option: Only one mode is primarily guided
questions.explanation: With only one spatial mode allowed (V < 2.405), there are no multiple ray paths to delay one another.

questions.question: If the wavelength increases while fibre radius and indices remain fixed, normalized frequency V:
questions.explanation: V ∝ 1/λ; longer wavelengths produce lower V numbers.

questions.question: For a fibre with greater NA, the acceptance cone is generally:
questions.explanation: Higher NA means larger sin(θmax), opening a broader angular cone of accepted light.

questions.question: If core-cladding index difference is reduced significantly, TIR guidance generally becomes:
options: Less strongly confined and NA decreases
questions.answer: Less strongly confined and NA decreases
questions.correct_option: Less strongly confined and NA decreases
questions.explanation: Lower index contrast Δ = (n₁ - n₂)/n₁ reduces the numerical aperture and makes the mode field more prone to bending loss.

questions.question: Which change most directly reduces coupling errors at a fibre input?
options: Accurate alignment of the source with the acceptance cone
questions.answer: Accurate alignment of the source with the acceptance cone
questions.correct_option: Accurate alignment of the source with the acceptance cone
questions.explanation: Matching the source emission angle to the fibre's acceptance angle minimizes geometric insertion loss.
